title.zh: 卷一百二十一 列傳第四十六 劉鍾崔二王
title.en: Volume 121 Biographies 46: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Kings
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 列傳第四十六 劉鍾崔二王 Volume 121 Biographies 46: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Kings

sentences.zh: 劉鍾崔二王

translations.literal: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the Two Wangs

sentences.zh: ◎劉鐘崔二王

translations.literal: ◎ Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the two Wangs
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Zhong, Cui, and the Two Wangs

sentences.zh: 劉幽求，冀州武強人。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu was a person of Wuqiang in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu was a native of Wuqiang in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，舉制科中第。

translations.literal: In the Shengli era, he was raised in the irregular-subject examination and placed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengli reign period, he passed the special imperial examination.

sentences.zh: 調閬中尉，刺史不禮，棄官去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant magistrate of Langzhong; the prefect did not treat him with ritual, and he abandoned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant magistrate of Langzhong, but the prefect slighted him, so he resigned and left office.

sentences.zh: 久之，授朝邑尉。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was given the post of assistant magistrate of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was appointed assistant magistrate of Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 桓彥範等誅張易之、昌宗，而不殺武三思，幽求謂彥範曰：「公等無葬地矣。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan and others executed Zhang Yizhi and Changzong but did not kill Wu Sansi. Youqiu said to Yanfan: "You gentlemen have no burial ground."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Yanfan and his allies killed Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong but spared Wu Sansi, Youqiu told Yanfan, "You have doomed yourselves — you will have no graves to lie in."

sentences.zh: 不早計，後且噬臍。

translations.literal: If you do not plan early, afterward you will bite your navel.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act now, you will regret it when it is too late."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " They did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: They did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 既，五王皆為三思構死。

translations.literal: Thereafter, the five kings were all framed to death by Sansi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, all five princes were framed and put to death by Sansi.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王入誅韋庶人，預參大策，是夜號令詔敕一出其手。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linzi entered to execute the commoner Wei; he took part beforehand in the great plan, and that night orders, commands, and edicts all issued from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi moved in to kill Empress Wei, Youqiu had helped shape the grand strategy; that night every order and edict came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 以功授中書舍人，參知機務，爵中山縣男，實封二百戶，授二子五品官，二代俱贈刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was given Secretariat drafter, participation in state affairs, ennobled as Baron of Zhongshan County with two hundred actual households, two sons given fifth-rank offices, and both generations posthumously granted prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Secretariat drafter with a voice in policy, ennobled as Baron of Zhongshan with an income of two hundred households, and both his sons were given fifth-rank posts; two generations of his forebears were posthumously honored as prefects.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，進尚書右丞、徐國公，增封戶至五百，賜物千段、奴婢二十人、第一區、良田千畝、金銀雜物稱是。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was established, he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Xu, increased enfeoffment households to five hundred, and given a thousand lengths of goods, twenty slaves, one top-grade residence, a thousand mu of good fields, and gold, silver, and miscellaneous objects in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Youqiu was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and created Duke of Xu; his fief was raised to five hundred households, and he received a thousand bolts of silk, twenty servants, a first-class mansion, a thousand mu of fertile land, and comparable gifts in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，以戶部尚書罷政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun, as Minister of Revenue he was removed from administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 711 he left the chief council as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 不旬月，遷吏部，拜侍中。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Within the month he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 璽詔曰：「頃王室不造，中宗厭代，戚孽專亂，將隕社稷，朕與王公皆幾於難。

translations.literal: The imperial edict said: "Recently the royal house was ill-favored; Zhongzong relinquished his generation; kin villains monopolized rebellion, about to fall the altars of soil and grain; I and the kings and dukes were all nearly in difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict read: "Not long ago the house of Tang was in peril. Emperor Zhongzong passed away, wicked relatives seized power and threw the realm into chaos, and the throne itself was nearly lost — I and the princes were all brought to the brink of ruin."

sentences.zh: 幽求處危思奮，翊贊聖儲，協和義士，震殄元惡。

translations.literal: Youqiu, placed in peril, thought to strive; he assisted and praised the holy heir, harmonized righteous men, and in shock exterminated the chief villain.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu rose to the crisis with resolve, supported the heir apparent, rallied loyal men, and crushed the arch-villain."

sentences.zh: 國家之復存，繄幽求是賴，厥庸茂焉，朕用嘉之。

translations.literal: The state's being restored to existence depended on Youqiu; his merit was luxuriant; I use this to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's survival rested on Youqiu alone; his achievement was outstanding, and I hold him in the highest regard."

sentences.zh: 雖胙以土宇，而賦入未廣。

translations.literal: Although enfeoffed with territory, yet tax income was not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Though he has been granted a fief, its revenue remains modest."

sentences.zh: 昔西漢行封，更擇多戶；

translations.literal: Formerly the Western Han practiced enfeoffment and again chose many households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Han, enfeoffment was often enlarged by adding households;"

sentences.zh: 東京定賞，復增大邑。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital fixed rewards and again increased great towns.
translations.idiomatic: under the Eastern Han, meritorious ministers likewise received expanded fiefs."

sentences.zh: 宜加賜實封二百戶，子子孫孫傳國無絕，特免十死，銘諸鐵券，以傳其功。

translations.literal: It is fitting to add and grant two hundred actual enfeoffment households; sons and sons' sons shall transmit the state without end; specially exempt ten deaths; inscribe on the iron covenant to transmit his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He shall receive an additional two hundred taxable households, his line shall hold the fief in perpetuity, he is granted ten exemptions from capital punishment, and his merit shall be recorded on an iron certificate to pass down to posterity."

sentences.zh: 」先天元年，為尚書右仆射、同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Xiantian, he was Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Same Rank as the Three Departments of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In 712 he became Vice Director of the Right Secretariat, a Grand Councilor of the second rank, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 幽求自謂有勞於國，在諸臣右，意望未滿，而竇懷貞為左仆射，崔湜為中書令，殊不平，見於言面。

translations.literal: Youqiu considered himself to have toil for the state, above the various ministers; his intent and hope were not satisfied, while Dou Huaizhen was Left Vice Director and Cui Shi was Secretariat Director — extremely unequal — seen in speech and face.
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu believed his service to the state placed him above the other ministers, and he was far from content when Dou Huaizhen became Left Vice Director and Cui Shi Secretariat Director; his resentment showed plainly in word and countenance.

sentences.zh: 已而湜等附太平公主，有逆計。

translations.literal: Before long Shi and others attached to Princess Taiping and had a rebellious plan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cui Shi and his faction aligned with Princess Taiping and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 幽求與右羽林將軍張暐定計，使暐說玄宗曰：「湜等皆太平黨與，日夜陰計，若不早圖，且產大害，太上不得高枕矣。

translations.literal: Youqiu with Right Imperial Guard General Zhang Wei fixed a plan, causing Wei to persuade Xuanzong: "Shi and others are all Taiping's party associates; day and night they plot in secret; if you do not plan early, soon great harm will be born; the Supreme One cannot rest his head high."
translations.idiomatic: Youqiu and Zhang Wei of the Right Imperial Guard devised a plan whereby Zhang would urge Xuanzong: "Cui Shi and the rest are Princess Taiping's partisans; they scheme day and night. Unless you strike first, great harm will follow — the Retired Emperor will not sleep easy."

sentences.zh: 臣請督羽林兵除之。

translations.literal: Your subject requests to supervise Imperial Guard troops to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to lead the Imperial Guard and eliminate them."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 未發也，而暐漏言於侍御史鄧光賓，帝懼，即列其狀。

translations.literal: Before it was launched, Wei leaked words to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin; the emperor feared and immediately listed the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be carried out, Zhang leaked word to Attending Censor Deng Guangbin; alarmed, the emperor reported the whole affair at once.

sentences.zh: 睿宗以幽求等屬吏，劾奏以疏間親，罪應死。

translations.literal: Ruizong handed Youqiu and others to officials; impeachment reported estranging kin by distance — crime deserving death.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong referred Youqiu and the others to the courts, which charged them with driving a wedge between father and son — a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 帝密申右之，乃流幽求於封州、暐於峰州、光賓於繡州。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly pleaded to vindicate them; then Youqiu was exiled to Fengzhou, Wei to Fengzhou, Guangbin to Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong secretly interceded on their behalf, and the sentence was commuted to exile: Youqiu to Fengzhou, Zhang Wei to Fengzhou, and Deng Guangbin to Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，太平公主誅，即日召復舊官，知軍國事，還封戶，賜錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: The next year Princess Taiping was executed; the same day he was summoned to restore his old office, know military and state affairs, return enfeoffment households, and was given one suit of brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Princess Taiping was put to death, he was recalled the same day to his former posts, placed in charge of military and civil affairs, had his fief households restored, and received a suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 開元初，進尚書左丞相，兼黃門監，俄以太子少保罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he was advanced to Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Yellow Gate Supervisor; soon he was dismissed as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director of the Palace Secretariat, but soon resigned as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 姚崇素忌之，奏幽求郁怏散職，有怨言。

translations.literal: Yao Chong had long resented him and memorialized that Youqiu, depressed and displeased in a scattered post, had complaint words.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong, who had long disliked him, reported that Youqiu, bitter over his idle appointment, was voicing grievances.

sentences.zh: 詔有司鞫治，宰相盧懷慎等奏言：「幽求輕肆不恭，失大臣禮，乖崖分之節。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to investigate; Chancellor Lu Huaishen and others memorialized: "Youqiu is frivolous and unrestrained, not respectful, losing the ritual of great ministers, violating the discipline of cliff separation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an inquiry; Chancellor Lu Huaishen and others reported, "Youqiu has been insolent and disrespectful, failing in the deportment owed a chief minister and overstepping the bounds proper to his rank."

sentences.zh: 」翌日，貶睦州刺史，削實封戶六百。

translations.literal: " The next day he was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou, and six hundred actual enfeoffment households were cut.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou and stripped of six hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 遷杭、郴二州，恚憤卒於道，年六十一。

translations.literal: He was transferred through Hang and Chen prefectures, died on the road in resentment and anger, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned through Hang and Chen prefectures, he died on the road in bitterness at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Minister of Rites; posthumous title Wénxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites with the posthumous name Literary Offering.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔與蘇瑰配享睿宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered him with Su Gui to receive paired sacrifice in Ruizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In 718 an edict ordered him and Su Gui to share offerings in Emperor Ruizong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 建中中，追贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, posthumously advanced to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously created Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 鐘紹京，虔州贛人。

translations.literal: Zhong Shaojing was a person of Gan in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shaojing was a native of Gan in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為司農錄事，以善書直鳳閣。

translations.literal: At first he was a recorder in the Ministry of Agriculture; for skill in writing he served directly at Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Ministry of Agriculture and, for his excellence in calligraphy, was posted to the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 武後時署諸宮殿、明堂及銘九鼎，皆其筆也。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time the inscriptions on the various palaces, the Bright Hall, and the nine tripods were all his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he wrote the inscriptions for the palaces, the Bright Hall, and the Nine Cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，為苑總監，會討韋氏難，紹京帥戶奴、丁夫從。

translations.literal: In Jinglong he was Director of the Park; he met the campaign against the Wei clan difficulty, and Shaojing led household slaves and corvée laborers to follow.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he was Director of the Imperial Parks; when the coup against the Wei faction came, Shaojing led household retainers and laborers to join the fight.

sentences.zh: 事平，夜拜中書侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, that night he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, participating in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was appointed that same night Vice Director of the Secretariat with a voice in policy.

sentences.zh: 明日，進中書令、越國公，實封五百戶，賚賜與劉幽求等。

translations.literal: The next day he was advanced to Secretariat Director and Duke of Yue, with five hundred actual enfeoffment households; gifts and grants matched Liu Youqiu and others.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was promoted to Secretariat Director and created Duke of Yue with a fief of five hundred households, receiving rewards equal to those given Liu Youqiu and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 既當路，以賞罰自肆，當時惡之。

translations.literal: Once he held the road, he took rewards and punishments as his own license; the age hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he dispensed rewards and punishments at whim, and the court detested him for it.

sentences.zh: 因上疏讓官，睿宗用薛稷謀，進戶部尚書，出為彭州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial yielding his office; Ruizong used Xue Ji's plan, advanced him to Minister of Revenue, and sent him out as Prefect of Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to resign his post; following Xue Ji's counsel, Ruizong promoted him to Minister of Revenue and sent him out as Prefect of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，復拜戶部尚書，增實封，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he was again appointed Minister of Revenue, increased actual enfeoffment, and changed to Heir Apparent Household Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong came to the throne, Shaojing was again made Minister of Revenue, his fief was increased, and he was transferred to Administrator of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 不為姚祟所喜，與幽求並以怨望得罪，貶果州刺史，賜封邑百戶。

translations.literal: He was not favored by Yao Chong; with Youqiu he was both guilty for resentment and expectation, demoted to Prefect of Guozhou, and granted one hundred enfeoffment households.
translations.idiomatic: Disliked by Yao Chong, he and Youqiu alike were punished for their discontent; he was demoted to Prefect of Guozhou with a reduced fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後坐它事，貶懷恩尉，悉奪階封，再遷溫州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he sat on another matter, was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Huai'en, all ranks and enfeoffments taken, and again transferred to Vice Prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, convicted on another charge, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Huai'en, stripped of all rank and fief, and eventually reassigned as Vice Prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年入朝，見帝泣曰：「陛下忘疇日事邪，忍使棄死草莽！

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he entered court; seeing the emperor he wept and said: "Has Your Majesty forgotten affairs of former days? How can you bear to abandon me to die in the weeds!"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan he came to court, wept before the emperor, and said, "Has Your Majesty forgotten what we did in those days? How can you leave me to die forgotten in the wilds?"

sentences.zh: 且同時立功者，今骨已朽，而獨臣在，陛下不垂湣乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, those who at the same time established merit — now their bones are rotten, yet I alone remain; does Your Majesty not bestow pity?"
translations.idiomatic: Those who won merit beside me — their bones are dust, yet I alone still live. Will Your Majesty show no mercy?"

sentences.zh: 」帝惻然，即日授太子右諭德。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved; the same day he was given Right Moral Instructor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and that same day appointed him Right Moral Instructor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷少詹事。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to Junior Household Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was made Junior Administrator of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，以官壽卒。

translations.literal: His years passed eighty; he died with the longevity of office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed eighty and died in office.

sentences.zh: 紹京嗜書畫，如王義之、獻之、褚遂良真跡，藏家者至數十百卷。

translations.literal: Shaojing was addicted to books and paintings; authentic traces of Wang Xizhi, Xianzhi, and Chu Suiliang — those who stored them reached several tens and hundreds of scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing was a passionate collector of calligraphy and painting; families holding authentic works by Wang Xizhi, Wang Xianzhi, and Chu Suiliang might own scores or even hundreds of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 建中中，追贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously created Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，韋後專制，畏禍及，更因僧普潤、道士王曄私謁臨淄王以自托，且密贊大計。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Empress Wei monopolized rule; fearing calamity would reach him, he further through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye privately visited the Prince of Linzi to entrust himself, and secretly praised the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, when Empress Wei seized power, Riyong feared he would be implicated; through the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye he paid a secret visit to the Prince of Linzi to place himself under the prince's protection and quietly endorsed the coup.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「謀非計身，直紓親難爾。

translations.literal: The prince said: "The plan is not to calculate for one's person — it is simply to relieve parental difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "This plot is not for my own gain — it is only to rescue my father from peril."

sentences.zh: 」日用曰：「至孝動天，舉無不克。

translations.literal: " Riyong said: "Ultimate filial piety moves Heaven; in undertaking there is nothing not overcome."
translations.idiomatic: Riyong replied, "Filial devotion so perfect moves Heaven itself — nothing undertaken in such a spirit can fail."

sentences.zh: 然利先發，不則有後憂。

translations.literal: Yet profit lies in striking first; otherwise there will be later worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you must strike first — otherwise regret will follow."

sentences.zh: 」及韋氏平，夜詔權雍州長史，以功授黃門侍郎，參知機務，封齊國公，賜實戶二百。

translations.literal: " When the Wei clan was pacified, that night he was edicted acting Chief Administrator of Yongzhou; for merit he was given Yellow Gate Vice Director, participation in state affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and granted two hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei faction was overthrown, he was named that night acting chief administrator of Yongzhou; for his service he was made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat with a voice in policy, created Duke of Qi, and granted two hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 坐與薛稷相忿競，罷政事，為婺州長史。

translations.literal: He sat because of mutual resentment and rivalry with Xue Ji, was removed from administration, and made Chief Administrator of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a bitter feud with Xue Ji he left the council and was sent out as chief administrator of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷揚、汴、允三州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through the three prefectures Yang, Bian, and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Yang, Bian, and Yun prefectures.

sentences.zh: 由荊州長史入奏計，因言：「太平公主逆節有萌，陛下往以宮府討有罪，臣、子勢須謀與力，今據大位，一下制書定矣。

translations.literal: From Chief Administrator of Jingzhou he entered to present accounts and thereby said: "Princess Taiping's rebellious conduct has sprouted; Your Majesty formerly used the palace offices to punish the guilty — minister and son's power must plot with strength; now occupying the great position, one descent of an edict and it is settled."
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Jingzhou as chief administrator to present his accounts, he said, "Princess Taiping's treason is already showing itself. When Your Majesty once used the palace guard to punish criminals, father and son had to combine counsel and force; now that you hold the throne, a single edict will settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「畏驚太上皇，奈何？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I fear alarming the Supreme Emperor — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I fear frightening the Retired Emperor — what then?"

sentences.zh: 」日用曰：「庶人之孝，承順顏色；

translations.literal: " Riyong said: "The commoner's filial piety is to receive and follow complexion and color;"
translations.idiomatic: Riyong said, "For a common man, filial piety means pleasing his parents' countenance;"

sentences.zh: 天子之孝，惟安國家，定社稷。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's filial piety is only to secure the state and settle the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: for a Son of Heaven, filial piety means securing the realm and settling the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 若令奸宄竊發，以亡大業，可為孝乎？

translations.literal: If you allow treacherous villains to steal and rise, thereby losing the great enterprise — can this be called filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: If traitors are allowed to strike and the dynasty is lost, how is that filial piety?"

sentences.zh: 請先安北軍而後捕逆黨，於太上皇固無所驚。

translations.literal: I ask that you first secure the Northern Army and afterward seize the rebellious faction — toward the Supreme Emperor there will certainly be nothing alarming.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the Northern Army first, then arrest the rebels — the Retired Emperor need never be alarmed."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及討逆，詔權檢校雍州長史，以功益封二百戶，進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was punished, he was edicted acting Inspecting Chief Administrator of Yongzhou; for merit his enfeoffment was increased by two hundred households, and he was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup was carried out, he was named acting chief administrator of Yongzhou; for his merit his fief was increased by two hundred households and he was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會帝誕日，日用采《詩》《大》、《小雅》二十篇及司馬相如《封禪書》獻之，借以諷諭，且勸告成事。

translations.literal: It happened to be the emperor's birthday; Riyong gathered twenty pieces from the "Major" and "Minor" sections of the Book of Songs and Sima Xiangru's "Fengshan Memorial" and presented them, using them to admonish indirectly and also urging completion of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's birthday, Riyong presented twenty pieces from the Major and Minor Odes of the Book of Songs together with Sima Xiangru's "Memorial on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices," using them as oblique counsel and urging him to complete the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 有詔賜衣一副、物五十段，以示無言不酬之義。

translations.literal: There was an edict granting one suit of robes and fifty lengths of goods, to show the principle that no words go unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded him with a suit of robes and fifty bolts of silk, signifying that good counsel never goes unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 久之，坐兄累，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time, he sat because his elder brother was implicated, and was sent out as Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, implicated through his elder brother's offense, he was sent out as Prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 後以例減封戶三百，徙汝州。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent his enfeoffment households were reduced by three hundred, and he was moved to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under the usual rule, three hundred fief households were cut and he was transferred to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元七年，詔曰：「唐元之際，日用實贊大謀，功多不宜減封，復食二百戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaiyuan, an edict said: "At the time of Tang's founding restoration, Riyong truly praised the great plan; his merit was great and enfeoffment should not be reduced — restore sustenance of two hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: In 719 an edict read: "At the restoration of the Tang house, Riyong truly aided the grand design; his merit was too great for a reduced fief — restore two hundred households to his income."

sentences.zh: 」徙並州長史，卒年五十。

translations.literal: " He was moved to Chief Administrator of Bingzhou and died, age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bingzhou and died there at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 並人懷其惠，吏民數百皆縞服送喪。

translations.literal: The people of Bing cherished his kindness; several hundred officials and commoners all wore white hemp and escorted the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Bingzhou cherished his kindness; several hundred officials and commoners wore mourning white to escort his funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰昭。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Minister of Personnel; posthumous title Zhāo.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel with the posthumous name Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 再贈荊州大都督。

translations.literal: Again posthumously given Area Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously created Area Commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 日用才辯絕人，而敏於事，能乘機反禍取富貴。

translations.literal: Riyong's talent and eloquence surpassed others, yet he was keen in affairs and able to seize the moment, turn calamity, and take wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong's wit and eloquence were unmatched, and he was quick in action — able to turn danger to his advantage and win wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 先天後，求復相，然亦不獲也。

translations.literal: After Xiantian, he sought to return as chancellor, yet he also did not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantian coup he sought to return to the chancellorship but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰「吾平生所事，皆適時制變，不專始謀。

translations.literal: He once told others: "What I have served in all my life has been all adapting to the time and controlling change, not specializing in the initial plan."
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "Everything I have done in life was adapted to the moment — I never clung to the plan I started with."

sentences.zh: 然每一反思，若芒刺在背」雲。

translations.literal: Yet each time I reflect, it is like awn and thorn in the back," he said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every time I look back, it feels like a thorn in my flesh," he said.

sentences.zh: 子宗之，襲封。

translations.literal: His son Zongzhi inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongzhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 亦好學，寬博有風檢，與李白、杜甫以文相知者。

translations.literal: He also loved learning, was broad and generous with moral bearing, and with Li Bai and Du Fu was one who knew one another through literature.
translations.idiomatic: He too was studious, generous in spirit and upright in conduct, and was known in literary friendship with Li Bai and Du Fu.

sentences.zh: 日用從父兄日知，字子駿，少孤貧，力學，以明經進至兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Riyong's paternal cousin Rizhi, style Zijun, was orphaned young and poor, studied hard, and through the Classicist examination advanced to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Riyong's cousin Rizhi, courtesy name Zijun, was orphaned young and poor; he studied diligently and, having passed the Classicist examination, rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 與張說同為魏元忠朔方判官，以健吏稱。

translations.literal: With Zhang Yue he was alike a judicial officer under Wei Yuanzhong in Shuofang, and was known as a vigorous clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Zhang Yue as judicial officer under Wei Yuanzhong in Shuofang and was known as an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 遷洛州司馬，會譙王重福之變，官司逃，日知獨率吏卒助屯營擊賊，以功加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Prefect of Luozhou; he met the disturbance of Prince Qiao Chongfu — officials fled, but Rizhi alone led clerks and soldiers to help the garrison strike the rebels, and for merit was given Silver Radiance Grand Master of Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Prefect of Luozhou, he was present during Prince Qiao Chongfu's rebellion; when officials fled, Rizhi alone led clerks and troops to aid the garrison in crushing the rebels and was rewarded with the title Silver Radiance Grand Master of Palace Service.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中少監，建言「廄馬多，請分牧隴右，省關畿芻調」。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Supervisor of the Palace; he proposed: "Stable horses are many — I ask to divide pasturage to Longyou and save fodder levies in the capital passes."
translations.idiomatic: Made Junior Supervisor of the Palace, he proposed, "The imperial stables hold too many horses — pasture them in Longyou to ease fodder levies on the capital region."

sentences.zh: 授荊州長史，四遷京兆尹，封安平縣侯。

translations.literal: He was given Chief Administrator of Jingzhou, was four times transferred to Intendant of Jingzhao, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief administrator of Jingzhou, was transferred four times to Intendant of Jingzhao, and was created Marquis of Anping.

sentences.zh: 坐贓，為御史李如璧所劾，貶歙縣丞。

translations.literal: He sat on corruption and was impeached by Censor Li Rubi, demoted to Assistant Magistrate of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of corruption and impeached by Censor Li Rubi, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of She County.

sentences.zh: 後歷殿中監，進中山郡公。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Supervisor of the Palace and was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Supervisor of the Palace and was advanced to Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 說執政，薦為御史大夫，帝不許，遂為左羽林大將軍，而自用崔隱甫。

translations.literal: When Yue held administration, he recommended him for Censor-in-Chief; the emperor did not permit it, and he was then made Left General of the Imperial Guard, while the emperor himself used Cui Yinpu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was chief minister he recommended Rizhi for Censor-in-Chief, but the emperor refused and instead made Rizhi Left General of the Imperial Guard while appointing Cui Yinpu himself.

sentences.zh: 隱甫繇是怨說。

translations.literal: Yinpu thereby resented Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpu therefore bore a grudge against Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 日知俄授太常卿。

translations.literal: Rizhi was soon given Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi was soon appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自以處朝廷久，每入謁，必與尚書齒，時謂「尚書裏行」。

translations.literal: Considering himself long placed at court, each time he entered audience he necessarily ranked with Directors — the age called him "acting Director."
translations.idiomatic: Having long served at court, he insisted on taking rank with the Directors whenever he attended audience, and contemporaries called him "Director in practice."

sentences.zh: 終潞州長史，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: He ended as Chief Administrator of Luzhou; posthumous title Xiāng.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as chief administrator of Luzhou with the posthumous name Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 王琚，懷州河內人。

translations.literal: Wang Ju was a person of Henei in Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju was a native of Henei in Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，敏悟有才略，明天文象緯。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was keen and perceptive with talent and strategy, understanding astronomy and celestial patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was quick-witted and strategically gifted, versed in astronomy and the patterns of the heavens.

sentences.zh: 以從父隱客嘗為鳳閣侍郎，故數與貴近交。

translations.literal: Because his father's younger brother Yinke had once been Vice Director of Phoenix Pavilion, he therefore often associated with the noble and near.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yinke had once served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, so Ju often mingled with the court elite.

sentences.zh: 時年甫冠，見駙馬都尉王同皎，同皎器之。

translations.literal: At the time he had just capped his years; he met Chief Commandant of the Horse Wang Tongjiao, and Tongjiao valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Still in his teens, he met Chief Commandant of the Horse Wang Tongjiao, who took a liking to him.

sentences.zh: 會謀刺武三思，琚義其為，即與周璟、張仲之等共計。

translations.literal: It happened they plotted to assassinate Wu Sansi; Ju honored his conduct and immediately joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in joint planning.
translations.idiomatic: When a plot arose to assassinate Wu Sansi, Ju admired the cause and joined Zhou Jing, Zhang Zhongzhi, and others in planning it.

sentences.zh: 事泄亡命，自傭於揚州富商家，識非庸人，以女嫁之，厚給以貲，琚亦賴以濟。

translations.literal: The affair leaked and he fled for his life, hiring himself out to a wealthy merchant's house in Yangzhou; recognizing he was no ordinary man, the merchant gave him his daughter in marriage and richly supplied funds — Ju also relied on this to get by.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed he fled, hiring himself out to a wealthy Yangzhou merchant who saw he was no ordinary man, gave him his daughter in marriage, and supported him generously — Ju lived on that patronage.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，琚自言本末，主人厚賫使還長安。

translations.literal: When Ruizong was established, Ju explained the whole story from beginning to end; his patron richly rewarded him and sent him back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Ju told his whole story; his patron gave him a rich send-off and sent him back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 玄宗為太子，閑遊獵韋、杜間，怠休樹下，琚以儒服見，且請過家，太子許之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was heir apparent, he idly toured and hunted between Wei and Du; resting weary beneath a tree, Ju appeared in scholar's dress and asked to visit his home — the heir permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was still heir apparent, he was hunting between Wei and Du when, resting beneath a tree, he met Ju dressed as a scholar who invited him home — the prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 至所廬，乃蕭然窶陋。

translations.literal: When he reached the dwelling, it was desolate and mean.
translations.idiomatic: At Ju's house he found only a bare, shabby cottage.

sentences.zh: 坐久，殺牛進酒殊豐厚，太子駭異。

translations.literal: After sitting long, they slaughtered an ox and presented wine of exceptional richness — the heir was startled.
translations.idiomatic: After they had sat awhile, Ju served beef and wine in lavish abundance, to the prince's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 自是每到韋、杜，輒止其廬。

translations.literal: From this time, whenever he reached Wei and Du, he always stopped at Ju's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever he hunted in Wei and Du, he stopped at Ju's house.

sentences.zh: 初，太子在潞州，襄城張暐為銅鞮令，性豪殖，喜賓客弋獵事，厚奉太子，數集其家。

translations.literal: At first, when the heir was in Luzhou, Zhang Hui of Xiangcheng was magistrate of Tongdi — by nature extravagant and acquisitive, fond of guests, hunting, and sport, he richly supported the heir and often gathered at his house.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the heir was posted in Luzhou, Zhang Hui of Xiangcheng was magistrate of Tongdi — a man of lavish tastes who loved guests, hunting, and sport, he entertained the heir generously and often hosted him at home.

sentences.zh: 山東倡人趙元禮有女，善歌舞，得幸太子，止暐第，其後生子瑛者也。

translations.literal: A Shandong entertainer Zhao Yuanli had a daughter skilled in song and dance; she won the heir's favor and stayed at Hui's residence — she was later the one who bore Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: A Shandong entertainer named Zhao Yuanli had a daughter skilled in song and dance who won the heir's favor and lived at Hui's house — she later bore Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 太子已平內難，召暐，拜宮門郎，與姜交、崔滌、李令問、王守一、薛伯陽等並侍左右。

translations.literal: After the heir had pacified the inner turmoil, he summoned Hui and appointed him Palace Gate Gentleman; with Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others he all attended at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir quelled the inner crisis, he summoned Hui and made him Palace Gate Gentleman; Jiang Jiao, Cui Di, Li Lingwen, Wang Shouyi, Xue Boyang, and others likewise attended him.

sentences.zh: 令問累擢殿中少監，守一太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Lingwen was repeatedly advanced to Junior Supervisor of the Palace; Shouyi to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen rose to Junior Supervisor of the Palace; Shouyi to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 此數人以東宮皆勢重天下。

translations.literal: These several men, through the Eastern Palace, all wielded power weighty under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Through their ties to the Eastern Palace, these men all wielded power across the realm.

sentences.zh: 琚是時方補諸暨縣主簿，過謝東宮，至廷中，徐行高視，侍衛何止曰：「太子在！

translations.literal: Ju at this time had just been appointed chief clerk of Zhuji County; passing to thank the Eastern Palace, he reached the court, walked slowly with head high; attendant guard He Zhi said: "The heir is present!"
translations.idiomatic: Ju had just been appointed chief clerk of Zhuji County and came to thank the Eastern Palace; in the courtyard he walked slowly with head held high until guard He Zhi called out, "The heir is here!"

sentences.zh: 」琚怒曰：「在外惟聞太平公主，不聞有太子。

translations.literal: " Ju angrily said: "Outside one only hears of Princess Taiping — one does not hear of an heir."
translations.idiomatic: Ju snapped, "Outside these walls one hears only of Princess Taiping — not of a crown prince."

sentences.zh: 太子本有功於社稷，孝於君親，安得此聲？

translations.literal: The heir originally had merit for the altars of state and filial piety toward ruler and kin — how can he have this reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has served the realm and honored his father — how has he come to such a reputation?"

sentences.zh: 」太子遽召見，琚曰：「韋氏躬行弒逆，天下動搖，人思李氏，故殿下取之易也。

translations.literal: " The heir hastily summoned him to audience. Ju said: "The Wei clan personally practiced regicide; the realm shook; people longed for the house of Li — therefore Your Highness took it easily."
translations.idiomatic: The prince summoned him at once. Ju said, "The Wei clan committed regicide and threw the realm into turmoil; the people yearned for the house of Li — that is why Your Highness won the throne so easily."

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，太平專思立功，左右大臣多為其用，天子以元妹，能忍其過，臣竊為殿下寒心。

translations.literal: Now the realm is settled; Taiping alone thinks to establish merit; left and right great ministers are mostly used by her; the Son of Heaven, because she is his elder sister by the same mother, can bear her faults — your subject privately feels cold heart for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is settled, yet Princess Taiping schemes for power, most ministers at court serve her, and the emperor indulges her as his sister — I tremble for Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」太子命坐，且泣曰：「計將安便？

translations.literal: " The heir ordered him to sit and, weeping, said: "What plan will be secure and convenient?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince bade him sit and wept, "What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」琚曰：「昔漢蓋主供養昭帝，其後與上官桀謀殺霍光，不及天子，而帝猶以大義去之。

translations.literal: " Ju said: "Formerly in Han, Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao; afterward she joined Shangguan Jie in plotting to kill Huo Guang — it did not reach the Son of Heaven, yet the emperor still removed her by great principle."
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "In Han times Princess Gai raised Emperor Zhao, then joined Shangguan Jie in plotting against Huo Guang — the plot never reached the emperor, yet Zhao still cast her off on principle."

sentences.zh: 今太子功定天下，公主乃敢妄圖，大臣樹黨，有廢立意。

translations.literal: Now the heir's merit has settled the realm, yet the princess dares reckless designs; great ministers form factions — there is intent to depose and establish.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has settled the realm, yet the princess dares plot rebellion and her faction among the ministers already contemplates deposing you."

sentences.zh: 太子誠召張說、劉幽求、郭元振等計之，憂可紓也。

translations.literal: If the heir truly summons Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and others to plan, worry can be loosened.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Zhang Yue, Liu Youqiu, Guo Yuanzhen, and the like to counsel you, and your fears may be eased."

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「先生何以自隱而日與寡人遊？

translations.literal: " The heir said: "How can the master hide himself yet daily roam with me?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked, "How can you hide yourself yet visit me every day?"

sentences.zh: 」琚曰：「臣善丹沙，且工諧隱，願比優人。

translations.literal: " Ju said: "Your subject is skilled in cinnabar sand and also adept at witty concealment — I wish to be compared to entertainers."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied, "I am skilled in alchemy and in witty disguise — let me pass as a court entertainer."

sentences.zh: 」太子喜，恨相知晚。

translations.literal: " The heir was pleased and regretted meeting late.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted and wished they had met sooner.

sentences.zh: 翌日授詹事府司直、內供奉，兼崇文學士。

translations.literal: The next day he was given Household Administration Rectifier, Inner Attendant, and concurrently Scholar of the Chongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ju was made Rectifier in the Heir Apparent's Household, Inner Attendant, and Scholar of the Chongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 日以諸王及姜皎等入侍，獨琚常豫秘謀。

translations.literal: Day by day the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others entered attendance; only Ju was regularly present for secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day princes, Jiang Jiao, and others attended the heir, but only Ju was regularly privy to secret counsel.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，遷太子舍人，兼諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he was transferred to Heir Apparent Attendant and concurrently Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Within the month he was made Heir Apparent Attendant and Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 太子受內禪，擢中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the heir received the inner abdication, Ju was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir accepted the inner abdication, Ju was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 公主謀益甚，幽求、暐謀先事誅之，侍御史鄧光賓漏謀，不克，皆得罪。

translations.literal: The princess's plotting grew worse; Youqiu and Wei plotted to strike first and execute her; Attending Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plan — it did not succeed, and all were guilty.
translations.idiomatic: As the princess's plotting intensified, Youqiu and Zhang Wei planned a preemptive strike, but Attending Censor Deng Guangbin leaked the plot; it failed and all were punished.

sentences.zh: 久之，琚見事迫，請帝決策。

translations.literal: After a long time, Ju saw affairs pressing and asked the emperor to decide policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis pressed, Ju urged the emperor to act.

sentences.zh: 先天二年七月，乃與岐王、薛王、姜皎、李令問、王毛仲、王守一以鐵騎至承天門。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, he then with the Prince of Qi, the Prince of Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi led iron cavalry to Chengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 713 he marched with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Jiang Jiao, Li Lingwen, Wang Maozhong, and Wang Shouyi at the head of armored cavalry to Chengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 太上皇聞外嘩噪，召郭元振升承天樓，閉關以拒，俄而侍御史任知古召募數百人於朝堂，不得入。

translations.literal: The Supreme Emperor heard uproar outside and summoned Guo Yuanzhen to ascend Chengtian Tower, closing the pass to resist; soon Attending Censor Ren Zhigu recruited several hundred men in the audience hall but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar outside, the Retired Emperor summoned Guo Yuanzhen to Chengtian Tower and shut the gates; Attending Censor Ren Zhigu soon rallied several hundred men in the audience hall but could not break in.

sentences.zh: 少選，琚從帝至樓下，誅蕭至忠、岑義、竇懷貞，斬常元楷李慈北闕下、賈膺福李猷於內客省。

translations.literal: After a short while, Ju followed the emperor to below the tower and executed Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen; he beheaded Chang Yuankai and Li Ci below the northern gate, and Jia Yingfu and Li You in the Inner Guests Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Ju followed the emperor below the tower and executed Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Yi, and Dou Huaizhen; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci were beheaded below the northern gate, and Jia Yingfu and Li You in the Inner Guests Office.

sentences.zh: 事平，琚進戶部尚書、封趙國公，皎工部尚書、楚國公，毛仲輔國大將軍、霍國公，守一太常卿、晉國公，各食實戶五百；

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Ju was advanced to Minister of Revenue and enfeoffed Duke of Zhao; Jiao to Minister of Works and Duke of Chu; Maozhong to Assistant State General and Duke of Huo; Shouyi to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Jin — each with five hundred actual households;
translations.idiomatic: When the coup succeeded, Ju was made Minister of Revenue and Duke of Zhao; Jiao Minister of Works and Duke of Chu; Maozhong Assistant State General and Duke of Huo; Shouyi Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Duke of Jin — each with five hundred fief households;

sentences.zh: 令問殿中監、宋國公，實戶三百。

translations.literal: Lingwen was Supervisor of the Palace and Duke of Song, with three hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen was made Supervisor of the Palace and Duke of Song with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 琚、皎、令問辭不就，以舊官增戶二百。

translations.literal: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen declined and did not accept; on their old offices two hundred households were added.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, Jiao, and Lingwen declined the new posts and kept their former offices with two hundred additional households each.

sentences.zh: 於是帝召燕內殿，賜金銀雜皿皆一床、帛二千、第一區。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor summoned them to feast in the inner hall and granted gold, silver, and miscellaneous vessels each a full couch-load, two thousand lengths of silk, and one top-grade residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then feasted them in the inner hall and gave each a couch-load of gold and silver vessels, two thousand bolts of silk, and a first-class mansion.

sentences.zh: 帝於琚眷委特異，豫大政事，時號「內宰相」。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor and entrustment of Ju were exceptionally special; he participated in great state affairs and was called at the time "inner chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Ju above all others; he took part in major policy and was called the "inner chancellor."

sentences.zh: 每見閤中，視日薄乃得出。

translations.literal: Each time he was seen in the privy chamber, he waited until the sun was thin before he could leave.
translations.idiomatic: Each audience in the privy chamber lasted until sunset.

sentences.zh: 遇休日，使者至第召之，而皇后亦使尚宮勞琚母，賜賚接足，群臣不能無望。

translations.literal: On rest days, envoys came to his residence to summon him; the empress also sent a palace lady to comfort Ju's mother, gifts arriving in unbroken succession — the various ministers could not be without envy.
translations.idiomatic: On his days off envoys still came to fetch him, and the empress sent palace ladies to console Ju's mother with gifts in endless stream — ministers could not help but envy him.

sentences.zh: 或說帝曰：「王琚、麻嗣宗皆譎詭縱橫，可與履危，不可與共安。

translations.literal: Someone advised the emperor: "Wang Ju and Ma Zong are both crafty and unscrupulous in horizontal schemes — fit to tread danger with, not fit to share peace."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told the emperor, "Wang Ju and Ma Zong are cunning schemers — useful in crisis, dangerous in peace."

sentences.zh: 方天下已定，宜益求純樸經術士以自輔。

translations.literal: Now that the realm is settled, you should increasingly seek pure and simple classicist scholars to assist yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is settled, you should surround yourself with upright scholars versed in the classics."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，稍疏之。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood and gradually grew distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and gradually distanced himself from Ju.

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史大夫，持節巡天兵以北諸軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and, bearing the staff of authority, inspected all armies north of Tianbing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Censor-in-Chief and sent with imperial authority to inspect the armies north of Tianbing.

sentences.zh: 改紫微侍郎，道未至，拜澤州刺史，削封戶百。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; before he reached his post he was appointed Prefect of Zezhou and one hundred enfeoffment households were cut.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, but before he arrived he was made Prefect of Zezhou and stripped of one hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 歷九刺史，復封戶。

translations.literal: He passed through nine prefectures and again had enfeoffment households restored.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of nine prefectures and eventually had his fief households restored.

sentences.zh: 又改六州、二郡。

translations.literal: He was again transferred through six prefectures and two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned through six more prefectures and two commanderies.

sentences.zh: 琚自以立勛，至天寶時為舊臣，性豪侈，其處方面，去故就新，受饋遺至數百萬，侍兒數十，寶帳備具，闔門三百口。

translations.literal: Ju considered himself to have established merit; by the Tianbao era he was an old minister — by nature extravagant. Wherever he held a regional post, leaving the old for the new, he received gifts reaching several millions; several tens of serving girls; treasure canopies fully equipped; three hundred mouths in the whole household.
translations.idiomatic: Ju counted himself among the founders of the dynasty; by the Tianbao era he was an elder statesman of lavish tastes. In every regional post he moved from place to place, accepting gifts in the millions, keeping dozens of concubines, sumptuous quarters, and a household of three hundred.

sentences.zh: 既失誌，稍自放，不能遵法度。

translations.literal: Once he lost his ambition, he gradually let himself go and could not follow laws and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Once his ambitions were thwarted, he gave himself over to excess and ignored the law.

sentences.zh: 在州與官屬小史酋豪飲謔、摴博、藏鉤為樂。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he drank and jested with subordinate clerks, petty officials, and tribal chiefs, playing dice and finger-guessing for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In office he caroused with clerks and local magnates, gambling and playing drinking games.

sentences.zh: 每徙官，車馬數里不絕。

translations.literal: Each time he was transferred, horses and carriages stretched for several li without break.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he changed posts, his train of horses and carriages stretched for miles.

sentences.zh: 從賓客女伎馳弋，凡四十年。

translations.literal: Following guests, female performers, and galloping hunts — altogether forty years.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years he ranged with guests, courtesans, and hunting parties.

sentences.zh: 李邕故與琚善，皆華首外遷，書疏往復，以譴謫留落為慊。

translations.literal: Li Yong was formerly on good terms with Ju; both were gray-headed and transferred outward; letters went back and forth, taking censure, exile, and lingering fall as satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong had long been his friend; both were white-haired exiles who exchanged letters and found bitter comfort in their shared disgrace.

sentences.zh: 右相李林甫恨琚恃功使氣，欲除之，使人劾發琚宿贓，削封階，貶江華員外司馬。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Li Linfu resented Ju for relying on merit and throwing his temper; he wished to remove him and had someone impeach and expose Ju's long-standing corruption, cut rank and enfeoffment, and demote him to Acting Prefect of Jianghua.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Li Linfu hated Ju's arrogance and sought to destroy him; he had Ju impeached for long-standing corruption, stripped of rank and fief, and demoted to acting prefect of Jianghua.

sentences.zh: 又使羅希奭深按其罪，琚懼，仰藥，未及死，希奭縊之。

translations.literal: He further sent Luo Xiyi to press his crimes deeply; Ju feared, took poison upward — before he died, Xiyi strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Luo Xiyi to press the case further; Ju took poison in fear, and before it could kill him Luo strangled him.

sentences.zh: 時人哀其無罪。

translations.literal: People of the time pitied that he was without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned him as innocent.

sentences.zh: 始，琚為中書侍郎，母居洛陽，來京師，讓琚曰：「爾家上世皆州縣職，今汝無攻城野戰勞，以謅佞取容，海內切齒，吾恐汝家墳墓無人復掃除也。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Ju was Vice Director of the Secretariat, his mother lived in Luoyang and came to the capital, reproaching Ju: "Your family's previous generations were all prefecture and county posts; now you have no merit of storming cities or fighting in the wilds — you take flattery to win favor; within the seas they grind their teeth; I fear your family's graves will have no one to sweep them again."
translations.idiomatic: When Ju first became Vice Director of the Secretariat, his mother came from Luoyang to the capital and rebuked him: "Our forebears held only county and prefectural posts. You have won no merit in battle yet curried favor through flattery — the realm despises you, and I fear no one will tend our family graves."

sentences.zh: 」琚卒不免。

translations.literal: " Ju in the end could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Ju could not escape her prophecy in the end.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, he was posthumously given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 he was posthumously created Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太平之誅，張暐召還為大理卿，封鄧國公，實封戶三百，進京兆尹，入侍宴樂，出主京邑，時人以為寵，然自以幹治稱。

translations.literal: At the execution of Taiping, Zhang Hui was summoned back as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, enfeoffed Duke of Deng with three hundred actual households, advanced to Intendant of Jingzhao — entering to attend banquets and music, going out to preside over the capital region; people of the time considered it favor, yet he was known for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Taiping's execution, Zhang Hui was recalled as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, created Duke of Deng with three hundred households, and made Intendant of Jingzhao — attending banquets within the palace and governing the capital without; contemporaries saw this as favor, though he was known for able administration.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子詹事，判尚書左右丞，再為羽林大將軍，三至左金吾大將軍，以年高加特進。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Heir Apparent Household Administrator, judged as Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, twice made General of the Imperial Guard, three times to Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, and for advanced age was given special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of the Heir Apparent's Household, served as acting Left and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, twice as General of the Imperial Guard, thrice as Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, and received special advancement in rank for his great age.

sentences.zh: 子履冰、季良，弟晤，仕皆清近。

translations.literal: His sons Lübing and Jiliang and his younger brother Wu all served in pure and near posts.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lübing and Jiliang and his younger brother Wu all held posts close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 暐嘗還鄉上冢，帝賜詩及錦袍繒彩。

translations.literal: Hui once returned to his native place to tend the graves; the emperor granted a poem and brocade robes with silk colors.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui once returned home to tend his ancestors' graves, the emperor gave him a poem and brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 乘驲就道，子弟車馬聯咽。

translations.literal: He rode post-horses on the road; sons, brothers, horses, and carriages linked throat to throat.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled by imperial post relay; sons and brothers followed in an endless train of carriages.

sentences.zh: 使者賜賚，敕州縣供擬，居處尊顯。

translations.literal: Envoys granted gifts; edicts ordered prefectures and counties to supply provisions; his dwelling was honored and prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys brought gifts; edicts ordered local officials to provide for him; he lived in conspicuous honor.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載卒，年九十，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he died, age ninety, posthumously given Palace Attendant with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 746 at the age of ninety and was posthumously created Palace Attendant of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 履冰，歷金吾將軍，季良，殿中監，俱列棨戟。

translations.literal: Lübing passed through General of the Golden Crow Guard; Jiliang was Supervisor of the Palace — both ranked with halberd guards.
translations.idiomatic: Lübing served as General of the Golden Crow Guard; Jiliang as Supervisor of the Palace — both bore the halberd insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 王毛仲，高麗人。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhong was a person of Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhong was a native of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 父坐事，沒為官奴，生毛仲，故長事臨淄王。

translations.literal: His father sat on a matter and was confiscated as a government slave; Maozhong was born — therefore from youth he served the Prince of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was convicted and enslaved to the government; Maozhong was born in bondage and from childhood served the Prince of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 王出潞州，有李守德者，為人奴，善騎射，王市得之，並侍左右，而毛仲為明悟。

translations.literal: When the prince left Luzhou, there was Li Shoude, a man's slave, skilled in riding and archery — the prince bought him in the market and both attended left and right, while Maozhong was clear and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince left Luzhou he bought Li Shoude, a slave skilled in riding and archery, and both attended him — Maozhong being the sharper of the two.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，王還長安，二人常負房箙以從。

translations.literal: In Jinglong the prince returned to Chang'an; the two men often carried quivers on their backs to follow.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era the prince returned to Chang'an, and the two often carried quivers as they followed him.

sentences.zh: 王數引萬騎帥長及豪俊，賜飲食金帛，得其歡心。

translations.literal: The prince repeatedly drew commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold talents, granting food, drink, gold, and silk, winning their pleased hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The prince often entertained commanders of the Ten Thousand Riders and bold spirits with food, drink, gold, and silk, winning their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 毛仲曉旨，亦布誠結納，王嘉之。

translations.literal: Maozhong understood intent and also spread sincerity to bind and recruit — the prince praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong understood his master's aims and won men over with sincerity — the prince valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 韋後稱制，令韋播、高嵩為羽林將軍，押萬騎，以苛峭樹威。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei assumed regency, she appointed Wei Bo and Gao Song as generals of the Imperial Guard to oversee the Ten Thousand Riders, establishing authority through harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei seized power she appointed Wei Bo and Gao Song as generals of the Imperial Guard over the Ten Thousand Riders, ruling them with harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 果毅葛福順、陳玄禮訴於王，王方與劉幽求、薛宗簡及利仁府折沖麻嗣宗謀舉大計，幽求諷之，皆願效死，遂入討韋氏。

translations.literal: Company commanders Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince; the prince was just then with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and Lizren-fu defense commissioner Ma Zong plotting the great design — Youqiu admonished them indirectly, and all wished to die in service; then they entered to punish the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders Ge Fushun and Chen Xuanli appealed to the prince, who was then plotting with Liu Youqiu, Xue Zongjian, and defense commissioner Ma Zong — Youqiu rallied them, and all pledged their lives; they marched in to overthrow the Wei faction.

sentences.zh: 守德從帝止苑中，而毛仲匿不出，事定數日，乃還，不之責，例擢將軍。

translations.literal: Shoude followed the emperor and stopped in the park; Maozhong hid and did not come out — several days after affairs were settled he returned; he was not blamed and was by precedent promoted general.
translations.idiomatic: Shoude followed the emperor into the park while Maozhong hid and did not appear; several days after the coup he returned unblamed and was promoted to general by precedent.

sentences.zh: 王為皇太子，以毛仲知東宮馬駝鷹狗等坊。

translations.literal: When the prince became heir apparent, Maozhong was put in charge of the Eastern Palace's horse, camel, hawk, and dog offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, Maozhong was placed in charge of the Eastern Palace stables and hunting yards.

sentences.zh: 不旬歲，至大將軍，階三品。

translations.literal: Within less than ten months he reached Grand General, rank third order.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he rose to Grand General of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 與誅蕭至忠等，以功進輔國大將軍，檢校內外閑廄，知監牧使，進封霍國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: Joining in the execution of Xiao Zhizhong and others, for merit he was advanced to Assistant State General, inspecting and correcting inner and outer stud parks, knowing the Pasturage Commissioner, advanced and enfeoffed Duke of Huo with five hundred actual households.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in executing Xiao Zhizhong and others he was made Assistant State General, placed in charge of all imperial stud parks and pasturage, and created Duke of Huo with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 與諸王及姜皎等侍禁中，至連榻而坐。

translations.literal: With the various princes and Jiang Jiao and others he attended within the forbidden precincts, even sitting on connected couches.
translations.idiomatic: He attended the emperor in the inner palace with the princes and Jiang Jiao and others, even sitting on shared couches with them.

sentences.zh: 帝暫不見，惘惘若有失，見則釋然。

translations.literal: When the emperor briefly did not see him, he was dazed as if having lost something; when he saw him, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor did not see him for a time he grew restless; when Maozhong appeared he was at ease.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，詔持節為朔方道防禦討擊大使，與左領軍大總管王晙、天兵軍節度使張說、幽州節度使裴伷先等數計事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan, an edict ordered him to bear the staff as Defense and Strike Commissioner of the Shuofang Circuit, and with Left Leading Army Grand Commander Wang Jun, Tianbing Army Military Governor Zhang Yue, Youzhou Military Governor Pei Youxian, and others he several times planned affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 721 he was commissioned with imperial authority as Defense and Strike Commissioner of the Shuofang Circuit and met several times with Grand Commander Wang Jun, Tianbing Military Governor Zhang Yue, Youzhou Military Governor Pei Youxian, and others to plan strategy.

sentences.zh: 毛仲始見飾擢，頗持法，不避權貴為可喜事。

translations.literal: When Maozhong was first seen adorned and promoted, he rather upheld law, not avoiding the powerful and noble — a matter for rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: At first, newly honored with high office, he enforced the law without fear of the powerful — a welcome change.

sentences.zh: 兩營萬騎及閑廄官吏憚之無敢犯，雖官田草萊，樵斂不敢欺。

translations.literal: Officers of the two camps of Ten Thousand Riders and the stud parks all feared him and dared not offend; even on official fields and wild grasses, woodcutters and levies dared not cheat.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of both Ten Thousand Rider camps and the stud parks feared him and dared not transgress; even on government land no one dared cheat the timber or fodder levies.

sentences.zh: 於牧事尤力，娩息不訾。

translations.literal: In pasturage affairs he was especially forceful; foaling and breeding beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself especially into herd management, and foals multiplied beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 初監馬二十四萬，後乃至四十三萬，牛羊皆數倍。

translations.literal: At first supervised horses were two hundred forty thousand; later they reached four hundred thirty thousand; cattle and sheep were all several times more.
translations.idiomatic: Horses under his charge rose from two hundred forty thousand to four hundred thirty thousand, and cattle and sheep multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 蒔茼麥、苜蓿千九百頃以禦冬。

translations.literal: He planted gongmai and alfalfa on one thousand nine hundred qing to guard against winter.
translations.idiomatic: He planted gongmai and alfalfa on nineteen hundred qing to feed the herds through winter.

sentences.zh: 市死畜，售絹八萬。

translations.literal: He marketed dead livestock and sold silk to the value of eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sold off dead stock for eighty thousand bolts' worth of silk.

sentences.zh: 募嚴道僰僮千口為牧圉。

translations.literal: He recruited one thousand Yandao Bo retainers as herd keepers.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited a thousand Bo retainers from Yandao as herders.

sentences.zh: 檢勒芻菽無漏隱，歲贏數萬石。

translations.literal: He inspected and restrained fodder and grain without leakage or concealment; yearly surplus reached tens of thousands of shi.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened control over fodder so that nothing was concealed, yielding tens of thousands of shi in surplus each year.

sentences.zh: 從帝東封，取牧馬數萬匹，每色一隊，相間如錦繡，天子才之。

translations.literal: Following the emperor on the eastern feng sacrifice, he took several tens of thousands of pasturage horses, each color one company, alternating like brocade embroidery — the Son of Heaven was gifted by it.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's eastern feng sacrifice he paraded tens of thousands of horses in companies by color, alternating like brocade — the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 還，加開府儀同三司，自開元後，唯王仁皎、姚崇、宋璟及毛仲得之。

translations.literal: On return he was given Palace Attendant with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies; since Kaiyuan, only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was given Palace Attendant of the First Rank — since the Kaiyuan era only Wang Renjiao, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Maozhong had received it.

sentences.zh: 然資小人，誌既滿，不能無驕，遂求為兵部尚書，帝不悅，毛仲鞅鞅。

translations.literal: Yet by nature a petty man, once his ambition was full he could not be without pride; he then sought to become Minister of War — the emperor was displeased, and Maozhong was discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was a man of low birth; once his ambitions were satisfied he could not restrain his pride and sought the post of Minister of War — the emperor was displeased, and Maozhong grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 及與葛福順為姻家，而守德及左監門將軍盧龍子唐地文、左右威衛將軍王景耀高廣濟數十人與毛仲相倚杖為奸。

translations.literal: When he joined Ge Fushun as marriage kin, and Shoude and Left Gate Guard General Lu Longzi Tang Diwen, Left and Right Majestic Guard Generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and several tens of others relied on Maozhong to act wickedly together.
translations.idiomatic: He allied by marriage with Ge Fushun, and Shoude, Left Gate Guard General Lu Longzi Tang Diwen, Majestic Guard Generals Wang Jingyao and Gao Guangji, and dozens of others leaned on Maozhong to commit abuses together.

sentences.zh: 毛仲恃舊，最不法。

translations.literal: Maozhong relied on old ties and was most lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong, relying on his long service, was the worst lawbreaker of them all.

sentences.zh: 中使至其家稱詔，毛仲不甚恭，位卑者，或踞見，迕意即侮誶，以氣淩之，直出其上。

translations.literal: When palace envoys reached his house proclaiming edicts, Maozhong was not very respectful; toward those of lower rank he sometimes sat with legs spread to receive them; if they went against his intent he immediately insulted and reviled them, using his breath to override them, directly above them.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoys came to his house with imperial orders, Maozhong showed little respect; toward men of lower rank he sometimes received them sprawled on his seat, and if they displeased him he abused them outright, browbeating them as though he stood above the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 高力士、楊思勖等銜之。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi, Yang Sixun, and others harbored resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi, Yang Sixun, and others bore grudges against him.

sentences.zh: 毛仲有兩妻，其一上所賜，皆有國色。

translations.literal: Maozhong had two wives; one of them was bestowed by the emperor above — both had national beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong had two wives, one of them a gift from the emperor; both were renowned beauties.

sentences.zh: 嘗生子，帝命力士就賜，仍授子五品官，還，問曰：「毛仲喜乎？

translations.literal: Once he bore a son; the emperor ordered Lishi to go and grant gifts, and still gave the son a fifth-rank office. On return he asked: "Is Maozhong pleased?"
translations.idiomatic: When his son was born, the emperor sent Lishi with gifts and made the boy a fifth-rank official; on his return he asked, "Was Maozhong pleased?"

sentences.zh: 」力士奏：「毛仲熟視臣曰：『是子亦何辱三品官？

translations.literal: " Lishi memorialized: "Maozhong stared fixedly at your subject and said: 'How does this son disgrace a third-rank office?'"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi reported, "Maozhong stared at me and said, 'Why should this child stoop to a mere third-rank post?'"

sentences.zh: 』」帝怒曰：「前毛仲負我，未嘗為意，今以嬰兒顧云云。

translations.literal: " The emperor angrily said: "Before, Maozhong failed me — I never took it to heart; now over an infant he looks down and speaks thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, "Maozhong has wronged me before and I overlooked it — now he scorns even my gift to his infant son."

sentences.zh: 」力士等知帝怒，它日，從容曰：「北門奴官皆毛仲所與，不除之，必起大患。

translations.literal: " Lishi and others knew the emperor was angry; another day, at ease they said: "Northern Gate slave officials are all given by Maozhong — if they are not removed, great calamity will surely arise."
translations.idiomatic: Lishi and the others, seeing the emperor's anger, said another day in passing, "The officers of the Northern Gate were all appointed by Maozhong — unless they are removed, great trouble will follow."

sentences.zh: 」後毛仲移書太原索甲仗，少尹嚴挺之以聞，帝恐毛仲遂亂，匿其狀。

translations.literal: " Later Maozhong sent a letter to Taiyuan demanding armor and weapons; Junior Administrator Yan Tingzhi reported it; the emperor feared Maozhong would then rebel and concealed the report.
translations.idiomatic: Later Maozhong wrote to Taiyuan demanding arms and armor; Junior Administrator Yan Tingzhi reported it, but the emperor, fearing Maozhong might rebel, suppressed the report.

sentences.zh: 十九年，有詔貶州，福順壁州，守德嚴州，盧龍子唐地文振州，王景耀黨州，高廣濟道州，並為別駕員外置。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, an edict demoted him to a prefecture; Fushun to Bizhou, Shoude to Yanzhou, Lu Longzi Tang Diwen to Zhenzhou, Wang Jingyao to Dangzhou, Gao Guangji to Daozhou — all as vice prefects appointed outside the regular roster.
translations.idiomatic: In 731 an edict demoted Maozhong to a distant prefecture; Fushun to Bizhou, Shoude to Yanzhou, Lu Longzi Tang Diwen to Zhenzhou, Wang Jingyao to Dangzhou, and Gao Guangji to Daozhou — all as supernumerary vice prefects.

sentences.zh: 毛仲四子悉奪官，貶惡地，緣坐數十人。

translations.literal: Maozhong's four sons were all stripped of office and demoted to vile lands; by connection several tens of people sat guilty.
translations.idiomatic: All four of Maozhong's sons were stripped of rank and exiled to harsh regions, and dozens were punished by association.

sentences.zh: 有詔縊毛仲於零陵。

translations.literal: There was an edict to strangle Maozhong at Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Maozhong was strangled at Lingling.

sentences.zh: 守德本名宜得，立功乃改今名，位武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Shoude's original name was Yide; after establishing merit he changed to the present name and held the post of Majestic Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Shoude's original name was Yide; after his meritorious service he received his present name and rose to Majestic Guard General.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇故主於道，主走避，守德命左右迎之至第，親上食奉酒，主流汗不敢當。

translations.literal: Once he met his former master on the road; the master ran to avoid him. Shoude ordered attendants to welcome him to his residence, personally served food and offered wine — the master sweated and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met his former master on the road; the man fled in fear. Shoude had his attendants bring him to his mansion, served him food and wine in person — the master sweated and dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 數日，入奏曰：「臣蒙國恩過分，而故主無寸祿，請解官授之。

translations.literal: Several days later he entered and memorialized: "Your subject has received the state's grace beyond measure, yet my former master has not a foot of salary — I ask to resign my office and grant it to him."
translations.idiomatic: Days later he memorialized, "I have received more grace from the state than I deserve, while my former master has no livelihood — I beg to resign my post and give it to him."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其誌，擢為郎將。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his intent and advanced the former master to Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his loyalty and promoted the former master to Commandant.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮宿衛宮禁，以淳篤自檢。

translations.literal: Chen Xuanli long guarded the palace forbidden precincts and examined himself with pure sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuanli long guarded the inner palace and held himself to strict integrity.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗欲幸虢國夫人第，諫曰：「未宣敕，不可輕去就。

translations.literal: The emperor once wished to visit the residence of the Lady of Guo; he remonstrated: "The edict has not been proclaimed — you cannot lightly go or stay."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to visit the Lady of Guo's mansion, he remonstrated, "No edict has been issued — Your Majesty must not go on impulse."

sentences.zh: 」帝為止。

translations.literal: " The emperor stopped for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 後在華清宮，正月望夜，帝將出遊，復諫曰：「宮外曠野無備豫，陛下必出遊，願歸城闕。

translations.literal: Later at Huaqing Palace, on the full moon night of the first month, the emperor was about to go out touring; he again remonstrated: "Outside the palace is open wilderness without preparation — if Your Majesty must tour, I wish you would return to the city towers."
translations.idiomatic: Later at Huaqing Palace, on the full-moon night of the first month, when the emperor meant to go out, he remonstrated again, "Beyond the palace lies open country with no guard — if Your Majesty must go out, I beg you return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 」帝不能奪。

translations.literal: " The emperor could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refuse him.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，謀誅楊國忠闕下，不克，至馬嵬，卒誅之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he plotted to execute Yang Guozhong below the gate-towers but did not succeed; at Mawei he finally executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he plotted to kill Yang Guozhong at the palace gates but failed; at Mawei he finally put Guozhong to death.

sentences.zh: 從入蜀。

translations.literal: He followed in entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor into Shu.

sentences.zh: 還，封祭國公。

translations.literal: On return he was enfeoffed Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he was created Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 及李輔國遷帝西內，玄禮以老卒。

translations.literal: When Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the Western Inner Palace, Xuanli ended his life in old age.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Fuguo moved the emperor to the Western Inner Palace, Xuanli died of old age.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：幽求之謀，紹京之果，日用之智，琚之辯，皆足濟危紓難，方多故時，必資以成功者也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Youqiu's plotting, Shaojing's resolution, Riyong's wisdom, and Ju's eloquence were all sufficient to cross peril and loosen difficulty; in times of many affairs, one must rely on them to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Youqiu's strategy, Shaojing's decisiveness, Riyong's wit, and Ju's eloquence were all equal to saving the dynasty in crisis — in turbulent times such men are indispensable to success.

sentences.zh: 雄邁之才，不用其奇則厭然不滿，誠不可與共治平哉！

translations.literal: Heroic and grand talents — if their marvels are not used, they are discontented and dissatisfied; truly they cannot be used together to govern peace!
translations.idiomatic: Men of towering talent, if their gifts are not employed, grow restless and discontent — they truly cannot share in governing a settled age!

sentences.zh: 姚崇勸不用功臣，宜矣。

translations.literal: Yao Chong's counsel not to use merit ministers was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong was right to urge that meritorious ministers not be kept in power.

sentences.zh: 然待幽求等恨太薄雲。

translations.literal: Yet in treating Youqiu and others, the resentment was too thin as clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his treatment of Youqiu and the others was perhaps too cold.

sentences.zh: 毛仲小人，誌得而驕，不足論已。

translations.literal: Maozhong was a petty man; once his ambition was satisfied he was proud — not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhong was a petty man who grew arrogant once his ambitions were met — hardly worth mention.
